Portfolio news brief — 10 September 2026

Notable price action
- Health Care Select Sector SPDR (XLV) is -3.2% over roughly three sessions (latest observed price: $165.9200).

Market and major-name developments
- Treasury yields hit multiyear highs on Thursday as traders digested U.S. oil prices crossing $100 per barrel again, overshadowing a tame inflation report. (CNBC)
- The Treasury Department on Wednesday said it will buy back up to $6 billion of government debt in an operation aimed at keeping bond markets functioning. The much-anticipated announcement triples the normal buyback operation and follows a statement Aug. (CNBC)
- Markets are set to find out Wednesday just how aggressive the Treasury Department's bond-buying program will get, as Secretary Scott Bessent dared currency traders to challenge him. The department is expected to announce around 11 a.m. (CNBC)
- The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams will face off tonight in Melbourne in the league's first regular-season game in Australia. All three major averages closed Wednesday's session lower. (CNBC)
- yields rose on Wednesday after the Treasury Department unveiled a debt buyback plan that's triple the normal amount. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note was up 4 basis points at 4.845%. (CNBC)

Cloudflare (NET)
- Shares of Cloudflare ( NET -0.82% ) rallied on Wednesday, up 10.5% on the trading day. While Cloudflare didn't report any company-specific news today, investors may be appreciating it as an ancillary beneficiary of Meta Platforms ' ( META -1.17% ) new Muse AI agent. (The Motley Fool)

NVIDIA (NVDA; VOO top-five holding)
- In its second-quarter fiscal 2027 release, Nvidia ( NVDA -2.45% ) said that it would pay a cash dividend of $0.25 per share on Oct. It marks the second consecutive quarter Nvidia is paying a $0.25 per share dividend -- up 2,400% from its previous quarterly payout of just $0.01 per share. (The Motley Fool)
- It would be an understatement to say that Wall Street is bullish on Nvidia ( NVDA -2.45% ) . The artificial intelligence (AI) chip manufacturer announced its second-quarter results on Aug. (The Motley Fool)
- Here are the biggest calls on Wall Street on Thursday. (CNBC)
- When it comes to artificial intelligence (AI), two names seem to get more airtime than their peers: Nvidia ( NVDA -2.45% ) and Palantir Technologies ( PLTR -1.83% ) . Over the current earnings season, investors have already gotten thorough downloads on how Nvidia and Palantir are performing. (The Motley Fool)

Bitcoin (BTC)
- It was a rough day to be an investor in risk assets. The S&P 500 dropped 0.59% , the Nasdaq fell nearly 1%, and Bitcoin gave back some of its recent gains as August's Producer Price Index came in hotter than expected, reviving fears the Federal Reserve might hike rates rather than cut them. (Decrypt)
- Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong discusses the Clarity Act and what greater regulatory clarity could mean for the crypto industry. He also explains why the Bitcoin trade has already hit bottom, expecting upside amid pressure in global bond markets. (CNBC)

Apple (AAPL; VOO top-five holding)
- In John Ternus' debut showcase as CEO, Apple unveiled a swarm of new products, including its first foldable phone called the iPhone Duo, as well as the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max with a larger screen. But the biggest news for investors from Wednesday's event may be the absence of an iPhone 18 without the Pro moniker. (CNBC)

Amazon (AMZN; VOO top-five holding)
- Amazon has ordered six additional launches from Europe's Arianespace as it builds out a satellite network to challenge SpaceX's Starlink, handing the continent's space industry a major commercial boost as governments push for greater sovereign capabilities. The Amazon Leo order, announced Wednesday at the International Space Summit in Paris, takes the total number of launches booked with Arianespace to 24. (CNBC)

Alphabet (GOOGL; VOO top-five holding)
- Google on Wednesday said it would invest at least 13 billion euros ($15.1 billion) into AI infrastructure in Finland, marking the tech giant's largest single investment in Europe. Finland has emerged as a key location for data centers amid the AI boom, with hyperscalers and developers eyeing its available land and power, which is in short supply throughout most of Europe. (CNBC)

Informational only — verify primary sources before making investment decisions.
Routine price moves and stock-picking speculation are intentionally excluded.
